title: Implementation guide for iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS
lead: Learn how the current Apple app configures playback, loads a source and changes the player UI. Try each setting in the native form, inspect its applied Swift code, then use the corresponding SDK configuration or API in your integration.

blocks.text: Integrate the Player and its view
blocks.summary: Create and retain the SDK Player, attach its view, and load a source in the SwiftUI app for iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS.

blocks.text: This guide follows the SwiftUI app in apps/ios/Showcase, shared by the iOS and tvOS targets. Player is the SDK playback instance; a view, layer or controller presents its video. PlayerConfig describes the instance, SourceConfig describes one media source, and PlayerViewConfig describes a PlayerView. SwiftUI is Apple’s native UI framework; it is separate from the HTML-based Bitmovin Player Web UI used inside the iOS player.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: The app supports English and Japanese through the system or per-app language preference. This guide uses captures from the English app. SDK identifiers, code and returned data retain their original spelling. The standard Player controls also depend on SDK and system language settings.

Here SDK means the playback library integrated into your app. API means the public classes, properties and methods you use to configure or operate it. The form is a way to try those APIs; PlayerSettings, SourceSettings and other Lab helpers organize the app’s state and are not additional SDK configuration types.

items: Complete Local setup and licenses, then build Showcase-iOS or Showcase-tvOS in Xcode. The app pins Player 3.128.0 and targets iOS/iPadOS 16.0 or later and tvOS 15.0 or later. Use the dependency versions in this repository when reproducing a result.

Allow com.playerlab.ios or com.playerlab.tvos on the Player license for the selected target. Configure signing for a physical device. Analytics uses a separate license; see Analytics / Observability in this implementation guide.

Run the app, choose VOD HLS under Source and press Play. Autoplay is initially off and mute is on. On iOS or iPadOS, use Expand player if the preview is compact. Check that Position beside the preview advances before comparing another setting.
Open Settings. After Apply, choose Code to inspect the configuration actually sent to the SDK. The code excludes unapplied drafts and replaces license values with placeholders.

blocks.caption: Applied Swift configuration in Code. Copy code uses applied values and license placeholders.

blocks.text: ContentView retains PlayerModel with @StateObject so a SwiftUI redraw does not create another player. PlayerPreview presents NativePresentationSurface, the source selector and current position. ControlPanel switches between Settings, APIs, Code and More while keeping their draft state. In a wide landscape layout, preview and workspace are side by side. The onAppear call loads a preset only if a source has not already been selected. Do not create a new SDK Player each time a SwiftUI body is evaluated.

blocks.title: Retain the player model across view updates
Load the initial source when the view appears
blocks.text: .onAppear { model.loadInitialSource() }

PlayerModel and NativePresentationSurface are Player Lab helpers, not SDK classes. The standard factory branch calls PlayerFactory.createPlayer(playerConfig:) or its Analytics-enabled overload. The default surface uses the SDK’s VideoPlayerView. A selected source becomes a Source through SourceFactory.createSource(from:) and is passed to player.load(source:). Follow the source links for the surrounding app implementation rather than copying a fragment as a complete app.

items.label: Screen and controls: iOS / iPadOS / tvOS

blocks.text: Configure PlayerConfig and SourceConfig
blocks.summary: Map form values to PlayerConfig and SourceConfig, apply startup and source changes, and configure initial tracks or FairPlay-protected HLS.

blocks.text: Choose the object by when the value must take effect. PlayerConfig is creation-time configuration: the SDK documents that it must not be modified after creating a Player. SourceConfig belongs to a media source. Runtime operations such as play(), pause(), volume or track selection act on the existing SDK instance. Changing a startup mute value and changing the current mute state are different operations.

rows: Playback → Autoplay / Start muted
PlayerConfig.playbackConfig.isAutoplayEnabled / isMuted

From the startup defaults, turn Autoplay on while keeping Start muted on, then Apply. A changed player setting recreates the player; check that playback starts automatically and remains muted. If all values match the applied configuration, Apply is disabled.
Quality and buffer → Maximum bitrate
PlayerConfig.adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate; whole bit/s, 0 means unlimited
Try 1500000 on an adaptive HLS source. Compare applied code and available/current quality through the APIs; this does not force a specific rendition.
Quality and buffer → Forward buffer
PlayerConfig.bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration; seconds, 0 uses SDK choice
Try 10, Apply, then inspect applied code and buffer state during playback. A target does not promise a fixed actual buffer size.
Source → URL, type, title, poster
SourceConfig(url:type:), title, posterSource
Change title without changing the media URL. Apply reloads the source. A title is metadata and does not create audio or subtitle tracks.
Start position → offset and reference
SourceConfig.options.startOffset / startOffsetTimelineReference
On VOD, use 5 seconds with Start. On live, use a negative value with End. The SDK can adjust the requested position to media boundaries.
Settings → Advanced SDK → Player, Source or view property
The corresponding typed SDK property, applied before creating/loading its owner
Search the exact API name, enable Override, enter a valid value and Apply. Disable the override and Apply to restore the basic form value or SDK default.

blocks.title: Map the form’s player settings to the SDK
blocks.text:
func apply(to config: PlayerConfig, callbackJournal: NativeCallbackJournal? = nil) {
        config.playbackConfig.isAutoplayEnabled = autoplay
        config.playbackConfig.isMuted = startMuted
        config.playbackConfig.isTimeShiftEnabled = sdkTimeShiftEnabled
        config.adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate = maximumBitrate
        config.bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration = forwardBuffer
        config.styleConfig.scalingMode = videoScaling.sdkValue
        advanced.apply(to: config, callbackJournal: callbackJournal)
    }

PlayerSettings is the app’s value model; config is an SDK PlayerConfig. The final advanced.apply call applies enabled additional settings after the basic fields, so an enabled override can take precedence. When comparing a basic field, check that an override for the same SDK property is not still enabled. Values typed into the editor remain drafts until validation succeeds and Apply runs.

blocks.title: Create a SourceConfig from the source form

blocks.text: Use HLS or progressive MP4 for local Apple playback. The preset catalog uses HLS. The Source type field determines how the URL is interpreted; an .mp4 suffix alone is not a substitute for choosing Progressive MP4. For seeking in progressive media, the server also needs suitable HTTP byte-range behavior. This app does not accept DASH for local Apple playback.

blocks.title: Choose reload or recreation from the applied values

blocks.text: effect(for:) is an app policy, not an SDK method. A changed PlayerSettings, including view overrides, recreates the Player and surface, then loads the retained source configuration. Source-only changes load a new Source on the existing Player. Both paths restart at the configured offset or SDK default and follow Autoplay; the app does not preserve the current position or playing state. Reset to applied (Reset at enlarged text sizes) only resets the draft. Selecting a source preset clears its custom source fields and initial track preferences while keeping player settings.
Select initial audio and subtitle tracks

blocks.caption: The initial audio-language field on iPad. The app applies this preference through SDK track-selection APIs, rather than a language property on PlayerConfig.

blocks.text: For audio and subtitles, begin with content that contains the required HLS renditions. In Settings → Tracks, enter an audio language such as de-AT and choose Automatic, Off or Preferred language for subtitles. The app matches the full language tag before its primary language, so de-AT may select de. Missing matches keep the SDK/OS selection. More → Tracks shows what the SDK actually selected. The test stream’s language labels identify test renditions; they do not imply a translated soundtrack.

For ordinary source loads, the app waits for both SourceLoaded (source loading finished) and Ready (playback can start) for the same source. In the tested Player 3.128.0, these notifications can arrive in either order. Remembering both avoids skipping language preferences when Ready arrives first. Selection happens once, so later track changes made by the user or through an API are preserved.

In the checked HLS startup, selecting during SourceLoaded was overwritten before Ready, so source loading alone is not sufficient. For preloaded playlist transitions that omit readiness callbacks, the app instead waits for the current source’s playback clock to advance before selecting once. In your integration, retain the event subscription, verify which source it belongs to, and remove it when retiring that owner.
FairPlay and protected sources

blocks.title: Protected media and external services
blocks.text: For FairPlay-protected HLS, enable SourceConfig.drmConfig = fairplay in additional settings, provide the certificate URL and the license service URL required by that service, then configure any request headers or preparation callbacks it requires. The form creates FairplayConfig; it does not provide a certificate, rights or a license server. Widevine/PlayReady fields in this Apple app describe receiver configuration and do not add local Apple support for those DRM systems. DRM means Digital Rights Management, the mechanism used to authorize access to encrypted media.
Change the player UI and native presentation
blocks.summary: Change Web UI resources on iOS and iPadOS, select native presentation and scaling, and customize tvOS System UI.

rows: Controls drawn over the iOS/iPadOS video
SDK Web UI or the bundled shared JavaScript/CSS factories
Theme → Default, Sports, Live (DVR) or Cinema. Then inspect additional StyleConfig / BitmovinUserInterfaceConfig settings.
tvOS controls and remote menus
Native System UI, not the shared Web UI
Additional SystemUserInterfaceConfig settings; for runtime SystemUiApi operations select the Native PlayerView host.
The app’s surrounding buttons, forms and text
SwiftUI ContentView, ControlPanel, ConfigurationEditor and ApiInspector
These are app code, not SDK theme settings. Edit the SwiftUI views and rebuild to change their layout or font.
The video host and its native behavior
SDK VideoPlayerView, bound SwiftUI view, PlayerView, AVPlayerLayer or AVPlayerViewController
In APIs → Host, choose Presentation in Host setting. Choose Presentation code in the same selector to inspect the corresponding SDK integration.

blocks.text: Web UI on iOS and iPadOS

For an iOS/iPadOS theme comparison, keep the same source configuration, choose Sports, and compare it with Default. Changing the mode recreates the Player and reloads the source; it does not preserve the playback position. Sports uses fictional sample information. The factory is selected by a JavaScript function name, while StyleConfig supplies the JavaScript and CSS resource URLs. tvOS sets userInterfaceType to .system and has no shared Web UI mode selector.

blocks.title: Load a bundled UI and select its factory on iOS/iPadOS

items: For a Web UI option such as the playback-speed menu, open Settings → Advanced SDK, search BitmovinUserInterfaceConfig.playbackSpeedSelectionEnabled, enable Override and choose its value. Keep StyleConfig.userInterfaceType set to bitmovin. Apply, open the player’s settings menu and compare the result with the applied Swift code.

For additional CSS, use StyleConfig.supplementalPlayerUiCss with a resource URL reachable by the Web UI. It adds rules to the selected base CSS. StyleConfig.playerUiCss replaces the base CSS, so use it only when supplying the required complete stylesheet.

To change the shared component layout or its own styles, edit packages/ui-shared/src/liveUi.ts or src/styles/ui-shared.scss. Build @showcase/ui-shared, run pnpm sync:webui, regenerate the Xcode project so its WebUI resources are included, then rebuild the iOS target. Changing generated files alone is not the source change.

After rebuilding, check the theme, subtitle visibility, track menus and relevant UI events with the same media. A CSS change cannot add a native SDK capability or make a missing media track available.

blocks.text: The Swift code below shows the optional overrides after the bundled theme is selected. The values dictionary is the app’s validated draft representation; your integration can assign the SDK properties directly before creating the player. A factory name must exist in the JavaScript bundle you actually load. Native System UI does not execute that factory or its CSS.

blocks.text: Native presentation and scaling

blocks.caption: The tvOS native configuration form offers Fit, Fill (crop) and Stretch. These affect the video inside its presentation area, rather than the SwiftUI form’s size.

blocks.text: Scaling is a separate choice from the controls’ theme. Fit keeps the whole picture with possible unused space; Fill (crop), mapped to SDK .zoom, preserves the aspect ratio while cropping; Stretch changes the aspect ratio to fill the bounds. Compare them with a video and display area of different aspect ratios. The main form applies StyleConfig.scalingMode during recreation. The bound SwiftUI, layer and controller hosts also expose a current scaling choice in APIs.

To integrate UIKit directly, open APIs → Host, choose Presentation in Host setting and select Native PlayerView. Choose Presentation code in Host setting to inspect the integration. NativePlayerSurface creates PlayerView with the retained player, installs a retained FullscreenHandler and embeds the view with constraints. On disposal it exits fullscreen, removes its listener registration and clears playerView.player. AVPlayerLayer and AVPlayerViewController use player.register(...) and unregister the same player/surface pair when retired. An AVPlayerLayer draws video but does not itself provide transport controls.

blocks.title: Embed a native PlayerView and retain its fullscreen handler

blocks.text: System UI on tvOS

For tvOS customization, use SystemUserInterfaceConfig fields such as showSeekBar or showInfoViews in additional settings. For runtime SystemUiApi menu/actions, first select Native PlayerView and keep the System UI engine. The app builds native menu/action objects from structured inputs; contextual and info actions accept actions, while transport-bar menus may be nested. Open the native controls to inspect the result. SwiftUI test buttons outside the player are still edited in ContentView rather than through these SDK settings.
Return remote focus to the workspace tabs

The tvOS code viewer gives each wrapped line remote focus so the whole example can be read. Navigating with arrow buttons can require moving through the long document or entering Apple's AVKit playback preview. In ControlPanel, onExitCommand on the editor content sets a SwiftUI FocusState to the selected tab. The focused modifier binds each tab button to this state, so Back/Menu gives that tab focus. The tab-row HStack also uses focusSection to group its buttons for directional focus. Left/Right and Select then switch workspaces without traversing the document.

Keep this handler on the editor content rather than the whole screen. Back/Menu on the tab bar keeps its system behavior. Changing focus or switching tabs retains the draft and the current Player; it does not apply configuration or recreate playback.

blocks.text: Integrate useful playback features
blocks.summary: Call runtime APIs, observe SDK state and events, and integrate offline playback, Cast, SharePlay, and OS playback features with their required hosts and services.

blocks.text: Use APIs for operations on an already created player. Operations accepts arguments and displays the selected target explicitly beside Run API; searching only filters the candidate list. Related SDK state and recent events support checking the effect. State → Refresh reads actual current values, and Events records SDK notifications. Host contains factory and presentation choices separately. A successful invocation means the call ran, not that an asynchronous action completed. Match state and completion/error events to the source and player under test.

blocks.caption: The Volume editor and its fixed Run API action. The argument and the SDK value read after the call are shown separately; Code opens the corresponding Swift call.

headers: Try it in the current app
SDK integration and result to inspect
rows: Playlist: reachable, compatible sources
More → Tools → Playlist; edit source drafts, load the playlist, then compare next/previous, add, remove or seek operations.

Each draft creates a typed Source. player.load(playlistConfig:) and player.playlist operations manage the queue. Read current sources and PlaylistTransitionEvent; submitting a draft alone does not load it.
Picture-in-Picture (PiP): supported OS/device and app configuration
APIs → Host → Host setting → Presentation → SDK SwiftUI with bindings, then enable PiP and inspect availability before changing active state. Native PlayerView offers its own PiP API operations.

VideoPlayerView binds enabled, available and active state to SwiftUI. PlayerView uses pictureInPicture configuration/APIs. Availability and activation are separate; enabling the option does not guarantee a floating video.
Background audio / Now Playing: suitable content and app capabilities
Search PlaybackConfig.isBackgroundPlaybackEnabled or NowPlayingConfig.isNowPlayingInfoEnabled in additional settings, Apply and test the app’s background behavior.
The settings configure playback and system media information. They do not grant an OS background capability or make all video background playback eligible.
Advertising: a valid ad tag and compatible ad backend
Search AdvertisingConfig.schedule in additional settings and read the accepted ad-item structure. Apply, or use scheduling operations for the current player.

The app creates SDK AdItem objects and passes the schedule to advertisingConfig. Inspect ad-start/ad-finish/error events and actual playback; an empty schedule or inaccessible tag cannot produce an ad.
Request handling: a request actually made by the SDK
Search NetworkConfig.preprocessHttpRequest or preprocessHttpResponse. Start with the supplied unchanged-object body, Apply and load the relevant source.

The app adapts a bounded JavaScript-body input to the SDK callback, then calls its completion handler. Inspect callback calls/failures in State. It is an app interpreter, not a JavaScript callback API supplied by the Apple SDK.
Live rewind: live HLS with a retained seekable window
Load Live HLS, start playback, then use a negative offset action in More → Live controls and return with Live edge.

The app sets player.timeShift within player.maxTimeShift and derives its display state. The app control switch and the SDK time-shift setting both affect the quick actions; no retained media means no rewind window.

blocks.title: Bind SDK Picture-in-Picture and scaling state to SwiftUI

blocks.text: Offline playback, Cast and SharePlay

blocks.title: Offline HLS: iOS and iPadOS
blocks.text: Apply an on-demand HLS source and its DRM settings in Settings, then open More → Tools → Offline HLS. Initialize OfflineManager at app launch using the saved settings; after changing process-wide startup options, close and reopen the app. Select the applied source as an offline asset, discover/select tracks, start the download and inspect progress, offlineState and events. Only after completion, create OfflineSourceConfig and load the cached source. The current panel is not provided on tvOS. Use a physical iPhone/iPad for download and offline-playback validation; the recorded simulator run initialized and discovered tracks but did not complete a media download. Offline FairPlay also requires the appropriate persistent-license service.

blocks.caption: The offline inspector obtains actual audio/subtitle tracks from the SDK. Track discovery is a preparation step; the download state and cached playback need separate confirmation.

blocks.title: Google Cast: iOS and iPadOS
blocks.text: More → Tools → Google Cast, configure the receiver/discovery options, and initialize casting before enabling RemoteControlConfig.isCastEnabled. Initialization is process-wide; changed options take effect on a full app restart, not a Player recreation. Receiver playback also needs a compatible Cast receiver, local-network permission and receiver-readable media/DRM. A custom receiver may require its Bonjour service entry and a native rebuild. Inspect initialized, available and connected state separately, then receiver playback events. The tvOS app does not include this Cast panel.

blocks.caption: Receiver and discovery settings in the iOS Cast inspector. They configure startup, rather than proving that a receiver has been found or is playing.

blocks.text: For SharePlay, choose More → SharePlay. Listen for sessions, then explicitly activate the current source’s activity if appropriate. Select an actual OS-created session and choose Coordinate current player or Coordinate and join. Configure matching SourceConfig.options.sharePlayIdentifier values for participating sources. The app’s coordination call is below; the selectedSession helper retrieves an OS session, not a fabricated object. Activation shares the current source URL/title. OS eligibility, Group Activities signing capability and an appropriate system session are required; participant state and synchronized playback must be checked on the participating devices.

blocks.title: Coordinate the current SDK player with a selected OS session

blocks.text: Events and owner lifecycle

When adopting an event handler, retain it for the lifetime of its SDK owner and remove it before replacing that owner. The Events pane can use listener or publisher transport. In the listener path below, player.add/remove are SDK APIs; playerApiListener and recordApiEvent are app helpers. The identity check prevents a notification queued by a retired player from updating the replacement player’s screen. The same principle applies to source and view listeners. Keep normal playback state handling separate from the bounded visible event history.

blocks.text: Integration FAQ
blocks.summary: Diagnose configuration resets, licensing, UI resources, track selection, and asynchronous operations using the applied code and SDK state.

blocks.title: How does the editor keep its layout while the keyboard is open?
blocks.text: SwiftUI GeometryReader reports less available height when the keyboard appears. Using that aspect ratio alone can switch a portrait editor to a side layout and move the focused field. This screen chooses the layout axis from its own window shape and available width, and uses the reduced content height to make room for editing. While typing, it hides help text and reduces vertical spacing to keep the input and Apply and Reset buttons visible. Rotation and window resizing can change the layout while retaining drafts.

blocks.title: Why does Apply restart playback?
blocks.text: The form compares applied configuration values and deliberately reloads the source or recreates the player. PlayerConfig is not mutable configuration for a running instance. For a current playback action, use the corresponding runtime API in Operations instead. If your own product must preserve position across recreation, capture and restore the appropriate VOD/live state explicitly; that continuity is not implemented by this form.

blocks.title: The app builds, but playback fails with a license error.
blocks.text: Compilation does not authenticate a player. Confirm that the selected target’s actual bundle identifier is permitted by the Player license used by that build, that the synchronized local configuration reached the target, and that the device can reach the licensing service. A locally overridden PlayerConfig.key takes precedence. Compare a reference HLS source before investigating custom media. Do not publish key values in a bug report or copied code.

blocks.title: Why do the shared theme or my CSS changes not appear?
blocks.text: Check the platform and selected engine first: tvOS System UI does not use Web UI factories or CSS. On iOS/iPadOS, the custom-mode branch needs both bundled JavaScript and CSS; missing resources leave the SDK default UI. Rebuild and sync the shared bundle before regenerating the Xcode project and rebuilding. Check for an enabled advanced resource/factory override, which is applied after the selected theme. Change SwiftUI font/layout in the SwiftUI view files, not the player’s CSS.

blocks.title: Why are audio/subtitles unavailable or reset?
blocks.text: A language field cannot create a missing track. Inspect availableAudio/availableSubtitles with matching media, then select after SourceLoaded and Ready have both been recorded for the intended source. The app’s startup handling is specific to its checked SDK/fixture, rather than a guarantee for every stream. Prefer native HLS subtitle renditions for a workflow shared by iOS and tvOS System UI; adding external SourceConfig subtitle tracks does not give tvOS System UI the same rendering route. Inspect the applied track selection as well as the visible captions.

blocks.title: Why do Fit and Fill look identical?
blocks.text: When the video and presentation area have the same aspect ratio, there may be nothing to crop or letterbox. Use different aspect ratios and check the active host. For the SDK SwiftUI with bindings, layer or controller host, the current scaling control also affects presentation; compare that value with the main form’s creation-time StyleConfig.scalingMode.

blocks.title: An operation succeeded, but the feature is not working.
blocks.text: Read State and Events after the call. PiP availability, Cast discovery/connection, SharePlay coordination and offline downloads each have platform, service or device prerequisites and asynchronous completion. A submitted call or an initialized SDK is not the completed feature. For view operations, select Native PlayerView where the app requests a PlayerView host; for tvOS menus also select System UI. Use actual receiver/participant/download state rather than the operation’s status message alone.

blocks.title: Why are live rewind buttons disabled or the position corrected?
blocks.text: Start playback and check that the source is live and exposes a usable retained window. Live time shift and Allow live rewind controls are separate switches. Negative offsets are distances behind the live edge, not VOD timestamps. The SDK may correct to available media boundaries. If paused media falls outside the window, the app returns toward the live edge; if the stream finalizes as VOD, it stops applying live-window recovery. These controls cannot restore media already removed by the origin.

blocks.title: Does an editable callback run ordinary unrestricted JavaScript?
blocks.text: No. Apple configuration callbacks use the app’s bounded plain-value interpreter, then adapt the result to the SDK’s Swift callback. Read the input schema, required return type and fallback under the field. Syntax is validated before Apply; invocation occurs only when the SDK reaches that callback. Host objects, asynchronous work and dynamic execution are unavailable. Inspect callback calls/failures, and include the public parser/interpreter resources and Acorn license notice when reusing generated callback code.

items.label: Screen and controls: iOS / iPadOS / tvOS

blocks.text: Add Analytics and inspect playback in Observability
blocks.summary: Enable the app’s Analytics collector, then find the matching playback session and inspect its metrics in Bitmovin Dashboard Observability.

blocks.text: After the player integration works, add the Analytics collector. It observes supported player events and sends playback data to the Analytics license configured for the app. The primary place to inspect collected sessions, audience and playback quality is Observability in Bitmovin Dashboard. The Apple app’s local event list is useful for integration debugging, but it is not the Dashboard and does not prove backend receipt.

The current app accepts an optional Analytics license through local setup. In PlayerModel.makePlayer, the Standard PlayerFactory path uses AnalyticsConfig(licenseKey:) when that value is nonempty; otherwise it calls the factory without an explicit Analytics configuration. The Core and Legacy factory alternatives return before this enabled branch. Use the standard factory when reproducing this app’s configured collection path. This is the actual app branch, not a claim that other integrations cannot attach collectors differently.

blocks.title: Enable Analytics on the standard factory path

items: Configure your Analytics license through Local setup and licenses, allow the selected app identifier for that license, rebuild and start the app. Keep account API keys out of the client app; the collector license is a different credential.
Play a known source, noting its title, device and playback time. Test a normal start, pause/resume and an appropriate seek; use real playback conditions when investigating an error or interruption.

Sign in to Bitmovin Dashboard, open Observability and select the same Analytics license. Choose the period and time zone containing the playback. Find the session through the available audience/session views and inspect startup, rebuffering and error information.

When comparing a changed PlayerConfig, keep the source, device and test action comparable, and retain the applied code. Use the shared Analytics chapters for metric definitions, Dashboard visualization, API queries and analysis with a language model; do not infer collected metrics from the number of local events.
